topics.topic: Credential newline normalization, control-character rules, and HTTP byte encoding
questions: Exactly which suffix is removed, and what happens with CRLF or multiple trailing newline characters?
Which Unicode code points count as control characters in a credential value?
Are credential values restricted to an ASCII-compatible header-value grammar, encoded as UTF-8 bytes, encoded using an HTTP library's legacy encoding, or refused when non-ASCII?
Which exact characters count as control characters: ASCII C0 and DEL, all Unicode General Category `Cc`, or a broader Unicode control/format set?

Exactly which trailing newline is removed, which characters count as control characters, and how is an accepted non-ASCII Unicode value encoded into HTTP header bytes and into the credential-echo byte sequence?

judgement.why: P10 already judges the same credential newline, character-grammar, and HTTP wire-encoding questions on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Credential value character grammar, control characters, whitespace, and wire encoding
precedent.why: The exact newline sequence, character repertoire, and HTTP wire encoding are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Disclosure class for executions or mapped outputs with no values
questions: What is the execution class when the execution names no inputs and no outputs, such as a failed inputless function or an outputless operation?
What class must proof and execution assign to an empty output list from a mapped operation, especially when the binding's declared output class differs from the input classes?
What disclosure class does an inputless execution with no outputs, or one that fails before producing outputs, have?

quotes: highest_disclosure_class: [BEHAVIOR] MUST return the highest member of classes by the declared order of = models.DisclosureClass (open, then business_confidential, then personal_data) and open when classes is empty; no input ever lowers the result.

advance_run: [SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT] A value port's PortRef names exactly one StoredValue; a mapped node's value output, once every element succeeded, is one StoredValue holding the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's value_schema as items, of the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input, published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change; when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is; only a list that is delivered, to a node or a flow output, is measured, and an output no edge takes fails nothing; a mapped node's file output is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, derived from the elements' NodeExecutions whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, since no record of its own holds it, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input; a mapped element receives the list element at its map_index as its own StoredValue of the map_over port's value_schema and the list's class, or the spooled file at that position.
judgement.why: The later contracts assign open to an empty class set and assign an empty mapped output list the highest class among the node's inputs.

topics.topic: Ordering and wave semantics for forced conclusions versus executable nodes
questions: When an executable ready node and nodes newly eligible to conclude `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed` coexist, which is processed first, and how are transitive waves of such conclusions interleaved with executable nodes?

When do nodes count as becoming non-executable "together"—after each individual conclusion, after one scheduler scan, or after computing the full transitive closure of skip and upstream-failure propagation?

After an execution changes several downstream nodes, must the kernel first exhaust all newly derivable `skipped_by_guard` and `upstream_failed` conclusions, or select the smallest ready executable node first?
For a chain of newly skipped or upstream-failed nodes, are all transitively determined records sorted together, or is each propagation wave recorded before deriving the next?

When executable nodes and newly forced `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed` nodes coexist, in what exact order are their actions and NodeExecution records produced, and is transitive propagation processed as one closure or in waves?

judgement.why: P18 already judges the same ordering question for newly forced conclusions relative to ready-node execution on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records relative to ready-node execution
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined, executions sorted by (node_id, map_index), with status running; after an operation element, whose concluding record effects wrote, the next RecordRunProgressChange holds the records it made non-executable.
precedent.why: The later run contract requires newly determined skipped and upstream-failed records to be written immediately after the element that determined them, before the advancement loop selects another executable node.

topics.topic: Unit and truncation basis for disclosed failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after truncation to `failure_detail_bytes_max`?
What does `length` measure: Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, UTF-8 bytes after truncation, or another quantity?
Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?

judgement.why: P4 already judges the same failure-detail length-unit and truncation-basis question on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Unit and truncation stage used for redacted failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later note specifies the UTF-8 byte length of the retained failure_detail.

topics.topic: Whether encoded or transformed credentials are forbidden in answers
questions: May an encoded or otherwise transformed service credential be stored and returned as an ordinary service value, or does State 0 require the kernel to prevent all representations of the credential from entering an answer?
Does the State 0 secret guarantee cover transformed or encoded representations of a credential, or only the exact credential bytes the kernel can recognize?
Does the no-secret-in-an-answer guarantee cover semantic or encoded representations of a credential, or only the exact credential byte sequence?

quotes:
- **Secrets** — service credentials and tokens live in the installation's
  protected configuration; they never enter a function, a flow, a trace or an
  answer.

Only that verbatim echo is
   searched for; a body carrying the credential in another encoding is kept
   like any other and is protected only by its class.
judgement.why: State 0 excludes credentials from every answer, while State 2 permits another encoding of a credential to be kept and returned under ordinary disclosure rules.

topics.topic: Agent-visible representation and metadata for personal-data file collections
questions: How is a personal-data `many` file reference returned to an agent: one digest for the ordered collection, or an ordered list of per-file digest/class pairs, thereby revealing its cardinality and order?

When a file list’s aggregate class is `personal_data` but some member SpooledFiles have lower classes, does an agent lose size, media type and spool facts for every member or only for members individually marked `personal_data`?

quotes: show_port_refs: [FIELD_PROJECTION] For each PortRef, in order, MUST produce one ShownPort with the same port name and one ShownItem per referenced item in order: a StoredValuesRef reads its StoredValue records with read_records using RecordsById, and a value carriage item becomes ShownContent with its value_id, its canonical JSON text read with read_value_bytes from a StoredValueSource and its class, a file carriage item becomes ShownFile with digest, size, media type, class, its value_id and no spooled_file; a SpooledFilesRef reads its SpooledFile records with SpooledFilesByKey and each becomes ShownFile carrying its full SpooledFileKey and no value_id; a FileFactsRef becomes one ShownFile per FileFacts with the class the FileFactsRef carries, no spooled_file and no value_id.

show_port_refs: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] This is the one masking rule of every answer: the owner receives every item in full; when reader is not of kind owner and an item's class is personal_data, MUST produce ShownValueDigest with the value digest and class for a value, or ShownFileDigest with the content digest and class for a file, and read no bytes for it (A07 rule 4).
judgement.why: The later surface contract returns one item per referenced file in order and masks each file according to that item's own class.

topics.topic: Readiness and executability exclusions for concluded or waiting nodes
questions: Must readiness also exclude a node that already concluded or currently has a waiting point? Without such an exclusion, succeeded, failed, skipped, approval-waiting and service-waiting nodes remain ready from their inputs and may be selected repeatedly.

Does this mean a waiting element is executable during the current request, or only that it may become executable after a later approval, resolution or resume? The former conflicts with the rules that the run rests and nothing advances between requests.
During ordinary advancement, is a waiting element excluded from readiness until the specific request that clears or retries its wait, or may the scheduler select it again in the same request?

judgement.why: P22 already judges the same scheduler eligibility and retry rules for concluded and waiting nodes and mapped elements on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Scheduler eligibility, semantic finality, and retry rules for concluded or waiting nodes and mapped elements
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the Run by identity, its pinned graph with read_flow_version, and its trace with read_records through ExecutionsOfRun, and derive every element's conclusion from the trace: a function element from its NodeExecution's status, an operation element from operation_element_conclusion. If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused. Otherwise it executes one node at a time until no node can execute, then writes the rest or end state in one RecordRunProgressChange.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] A function element is executed with execute_function_element; an operation element is reached with reach_operation_element, given a RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError; operation elements that wait are not reached again here.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.

advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
precedent.why: The later run contract derives semantic conclusions from the trace, excludes waiting operation elements from ordinary advancement, forbids re-executing concluded elements, and classifies resolved `not_applied` as waiting for approval.

topics.topic: Startup behavior when credential-header collision facts are unavailable
questions: Must startup read every selected service's manifest instance to check credential-header collisions, and if so, does a missing or malformed manifest record stop startup or defer the failure to proposal/send time?
What must startup do when it cannot obtain the manifest instance facts needed to perform the mandatory credential-header collision check?

judgement.why: P23 already judges the same startup manifest-loading and credential-header-collision question on unchanged passages.

precedent.topic: Startup validation and loading requirements for selected manifest instances
quotes:
No credential header has, case-insensitively, the name of a required header of
its instance or one of `KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES`, `host` included; reads
installation and manifest only (A09 rule 1). The services checked are those the
installation holds a credential for, in `service_id` code-point order; for
each, the kernel-set names are compared first, without reading the manifest;
then, only when the installation selects an instance for it, its manifest
record is read and that instance's required headers compared. A service with
no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name,
fails nothing here: it is not invocable at send (A09 rule 6).

`refused` naming the first failing service, services taken in `service_id`
code-point order and each one's manifest record read in its turn — an
unreadable record, or one failing a check of the record itself (A08 rule 5),
fails at its service; the start stops.
precedent.why: The later startup contract specifies which credential-bearing services require manifest reads, when manifest faults stop startup, and that a missing selected-instance name does not stop startup but makes the service uninvocable.

topics.topic: Behavior when the configured service instance is absent from the manifest
questions: What happens when configuration names an instance that does not exist in the configured manifest revision: does the kernel refuse to start, treat the service as having no selected instance, or retain the name and fail later as an address-missing instance?

topics.topic: Deterministic failure detail when multiple outputs are invalid
questions: Which failing port or list element determines the recorded failure detail when several produced outputs are invalid?

topics.topic: Durable representation of a mapped file list's aggregate disclosure class
questions: Where is the aggregate disclosure class of a mapped `many` file output represented durably, especially for an empty list, so recovery and disclosure checks can reproduce it?

topics.topic: Indexing convention for mapped-element identity
questions: Is `map_index` zero-based, one-based, or another stable representation of list position?

topics.topic: Precedence between guard-based skipping and later upstream failure
questions: If one required input is already permanently disabled by a guard while another required input is still waiting and later fails, is the node skipped immediately, held undecided so it can become `upstream_failed`, or decided by whichever condition becomes known first?

topics.topic: Scheduling priority when resuming a partially processed mapped node
questions: What constitutes a new pass after a crash or after one or more mapped elements stop waiting, and does the partially processed mapped node resume before or compete by `node_id` with other ready nodes?

topics.topic: Scope of approval-preview redaction when an input is personal data
questions: When any input is personal data, is only the built-request field replaced by its digest while service metadata and individually redacted inputs remain visible, or is the entire preview reduced to the request digest?

topics.topic: Secret-handling guarantees for owner and agent tokens
questions: May owner or agent tokens appear in logs, internal-error diagnostics, stored request data or process arguments, or must they receive the same handling guarantees as service credential values?

topics.topic: Security checks required when rereading configuration after startup
questions: If the configuration file's ownership, permissions, regular-file status or path components change after startup, must a token-list re-read reject it or accept it after only A16's four checks?

topics.topic: Versioned size ceiling used to derive mapped-list failures during recovery
questions: Which ceiling must later readers and startup recovery use when deriving an unrecorded mapped-list failure from an older run?

topics.topic: Whether credential secrecy follows provenance or coincidental byte equality
questions: Is the prohibition based on secret provenance, or must the kernel reject or redact every unrelated value whose bytes happen to equal or contain a credential?

topics.topic: Whether the credential size limit applies before or after newline removal
questions: Is the credential size ceiling applied to the raw file bytes including the removable trailing newline, or to the credential value after removing that newline?
